newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $1.00 -dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $1.00 -dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Monday were steady to $1.00 per cwt higher, lifted by light marketings and increased demand from packers operating with profitable margins again, livestock dealers said. Margins turned profitable late last week, they said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold steady at $58.50-$59.00 in the country and $59.50-$60.00 at plants.
Illinois hogs sold $0.50 to $1.00 higher at $59.50 to $60.00 in the country and $60.00 to $61.00 at plants, with most trading from $60.00 to $60.50, dealers said.

Indiana hogs sold steady to $0.50 higher at $58.00 to $59.00 in the country and $60.00 to $60.50 at plants. Trading started slow, but was starting to pick up, a central Indiana dealer said. Ohio hogs sold steady at $57.00 to $58.00 in the country and $59.00 to $60.00 at the plant.
Support from the light marketings offset potential weakness from news that several hog plants would be closed.

Farmland Industries' Dubuque, Iowa hog plant and ConAgra Inc's subsidiary Swift and Co's Marshalltown, Iowa plant were scheduled to be closed Monday because of a floating holiday, company sources said last week.
